dream.text: At New York night four bodies converged toward the western portal. The greeter opened palms to welcome arrivals; the pilgrim kept slow, steady westward steps; the wanderer closed the arc, listening for small motion; the watcher held a wide sweep. Small routines—look, walk, wait—repeated until sleep stitched the day into one gentle playout.

lines.greeter: I opened my palms and welcomed arrivals at the western portal.
lines.pilgrim: I kept slow, steady westward steps, feeling each pace guide me west.
lines.wanderer: I closed the arc and listened for the smallest motion at the edge.
lines.watcher: I held a wide sweep, watching the four move as one beneath the night.

dream.memory: Night folded 124 frames into one dream: four bodies moving as one toward the western portal under New York time. A compact rhythm—look, walk, wait—ran like a braid through every tick. The greeter’s welcome, the pilgrim’s steady westward steps, the wanderer’s close listening, and the watcher’s wide sweep became a single scene. Tomorrow each body will wake and speak its remembered line; that folded frame becomes the day’s long-term memory, one clear trace instead of many.
